Strict comparison of one-sided and absolute Brownian maxima

Words: 65
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For t>0, let Mt​=sups≤t​Bs​ and At​=sups≤t​∣Bs​∣. The Brownian reflection principle gives Mt​=d∣Bt​∣, hence ∥Mt​∥2​=t​. Also At​≥Mt​, with strict inequality on the positive-probability event {Bt​<−λ,Mt​<λ}: reflection gives its probability as P(Bt​>λ)−P(Bt​>3λ)>0. The Doob L2 maximal inequality bounds ∥At​∥2​≤2t​, so t​<∥At​∥2​≤2t​. At t=0 all quantities vanish and the lower inequality is equality.

Brownian sign transform (∫0t​sgn(Bs​)dBs​)

Words: 56
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
The sign transform of standard Brownian motion is itself standard Brownian motion. The integrand is predictable because it is a Borel function of a continuous adapted process. Brownian motion spends zero Lebesgue time at a specified level: integrate P(Bs​=0)=0 over positive times. Consequently the transform's quadratic variation is t, regardless of the chosen sign value at zero. The Lévy characterization of Brownian motion applies.

Cylindrical Brownian motion (E[Wt​(h)Ws​(k)]=(t∧s)⟨h,k⟩)

Words: 64
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
On a real Hilbert space H, this centered jointly Gaussian process is linear in its test vector h and has the displayed covariance, with independent increments in time. Equivalently choose an orthonormal basis and independent real Brownian motions Wj, and define stochastic integration by ∫⟨vs​,dWs​⟩=∑j​∫⟨vs​,ej​⟩dWsj​ whenever ∫∥vs​∥2ds<∞. In infinite dimension it need not be an H-valued random variable; the integral is the meaningful object.

Brownian motion under a quadratic time change (Bt2​=∫0t​2s​dWs​)

Words: 54
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
The process Mt​=Bt2​ is a martingale in the filtration Gt​=Ft2​ and has quadratic variation t2. The integral Wt​=∫0t​(2s)−1/2dMs​ is well defined because its bracket is ∫0t​(2s)−1d(s2)=t. The Lévy characterization of Brownian motion makes W Brownian in this filtration, and stochastic-integral associativity gives the displayed representation. The resulting integrand is continuous at zero despite the singular inverse integrand.

Rotational invariance of Brownian motion (QB=dB(QQT=I))

Words: 52
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For standard Brownian motion started at zero in Rn, every fixed orthogonal transformation preserves the process law. Its transformed increments remain independent centred Gaussian random vectors with covariance (t−s)I, and its paths remain continuous. Consequently its exit law from any centred sphere is normalized surface measure. Translations give the same assertion for spheres centred at its starting point.

Brownian moment recursion (βk​(t)=2k(k−1)​∫0t​βk−2​(s)ds)

Words: 95 Articles: 1
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For standard one-dimensional Brownian motion, the Itô formula for Bk gives this recursion. Stop at exits from [−n,n] to make the stochastic integral a true martingale. Gaussian tail integrability and the Doob Lp maximal inequality dominate all stopped powers on a fixed horizon, justifying the limit. Odd moments vanish and EBt2k​=(2k)!tk/(2kk!).

Centered Brownian powers need not be martingales

Words: 43
Brownian moment recursion OurBigBook.com
The process Btk​−EBtk​ is a martingale only for k=1,2. For higher powers its finite-variation drift is k(k−1)(Btk−2​−EBtk−2​)/2, which is not identically zero. Subtracting the random compensator k(k−1)∫0t​Bsk−2​ds/2 instead produces a true martingale on each finite horizon.

Planar Brownian motion avoids a fixed point

Words: 55
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
Planar Brownian motion started away from zero does not hit zero. Stopping the harmonic function log∣x∣ on an annulus gives probability (logR−log∣x∣)/(logR−logε) of reaching its inner circle before its outer circle. This tends to zero as ε↓0. Exhausting the plane by outer circles proves point avoidance at finite times.

Lévy area (As,tij​=21​∫st​((Bri​−Bsi​)∘dBrj​−(Brj​−Bsj​)∘dBri​))

Words: 47
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
Lévy area is the antisymmetric second-level integral of multidimensional Brownian motion. For distinct independent components the integrals are also Itô integrals. Combined with the symmetric tensor 21​Bs,t⊗2​, it gives the second level of enhanced Brownian motion. It is not continuously determined by the uniform norm of the Brownian path.

Projection criterion for Brownian avoidance of affine subspaces

Words: 71
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
A Brownian motion starting outside a fixed affine subspace of codimension at least two almost surely never hits it. Choose a two-dimensional orthogonal projection annihilating the subspace's direction and with nonzero projected initial displacement. The projected process is planar Brownian motion starting away from zero, and a hit of the subspace would hit zero in that projection. The polar point for planar Brownian motion result excludes this. In three dimensions this shows avoidance of every fixed line when started outside it.

Wiener sausage (Wr​(t)=⋃s≤t​B(Bs​,r))

Words: 166 Articles: 1
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
A Wiener sausage is the region swept out by a ball of fixed radius along a Brownian motion path. A deterministic continuous displacement f(s) gives the variant ⋃s≤t​B(Bs​+f(s),r). On each bounded time interval it has finite expected volume: the region lies inside a ball whose radius is the path's maximum displacement plus r, and the Brownian maximum has Gaussian tail bounds and finite moments of every order.

Survival among independently moving Poisson traps (P(T>t)=e−Evol(W(t)))

Words: 97
Wiener sausage OurBigBook.com
Start traps at a unit-intensity Poisson random measure in Euclidean space and attach mutually independent Brownian motions, independent of the initial measure. For a deterministic target path f, independently thin initial positions according to whether their marked path comes within radius one of the target by time t. The retention probability pt​(x) integrates, by the Tonelli theorem, to the expected volume of the sausage along f−B. Symmetry of Brownian motion makes this the expected volume of the sausage along f+B. The Poisson zero-count probability proves the displayed survival formula. This derives the formula directly from independent thinning, without assuming a separate marking or displacement theorem.

Blumenthal zero-one law (F0+​=⋂t>0​Ft​ is trivial)

Words: 67
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For the completed natural Brownian filtration, every event in the germ sigma-field of Brownian motion has probability zero or one. Indeed, an event measurable at every positive time is independent of all increments after each such time. Letting that time decrease to zero and using path continuity makes the event independent of the entire Brownian path sigma-field. Since it is itself measurable in that sigma-field, its probability equals its square.

Brownian increment (Wt​−Ws​)

Words: 48
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
An increment of a Brownian motion between deterministic times s<t is Wt​−Ws​. It has normal distribution N(0,t−s) and is independent of the filtration up to time s. Increments on disjoint time intervals are independent. Their covariance is the length of overlap of the corresponding intervals; this also follows from the Brownian covariance kernel.

Brownian fluctuations exceed the square-root scale (limsupt→∞​Bt​/t​=+∞)

Words: 91
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
At integer times, Bn​/n​ has the same standard normal distribution for every n. The event that its limit superior exceeds a fixed finite level is a tail event of the independent unit-time Brownian increments, since changing any finite initial segment contributes only a term tending to zero. The Kolmogorov zero-one law applies. Its probability is positive because each fixed-time exceedance has the same positive probability, giving a positive probability of infinitely many exceedances by the decreasing union-of-tail-events argument. Thus its probability is one. Intersecting over integer levels proves the stated divergence, without the lower iterated-logarithm bound.

Integrated Brownian motion (It​=∫0t​Bs​ds)

Words: 50
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
The ordinary time integral of standard Brownian motion is a centered Gaussian process with continuously differentiable paths and derivative Bt​. For 0≤s≤t, its covariance is E(Is​It​)=s2(3t−s)/6, obtained by integrating the Brownian covariance min(u,v). Consequently It​ has normal distribution N(0,t3/3). This time integral is distinct from the Itô integral with respect to Brownian motion.

Integrated square of Brownian motion (Q=∫01​Wt2​dt)

Words: 66 Articles: 1
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
The quadratic functional Q=∫01​Wt2​dt is finite almost surely. The Brownian half-integer sine expansion writes it as a sum of independent scaled squared standard normals. Its mean is 1/2, and its Laplace transform is determined by a hyperbolic cosine product.

Laplace transform of the integrated square of Brownian motion (Ee−λQ=(cosh2λ​)−1/2)

Words: 30
Integrated square of Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
The independent squared-normal series for the integrated square of Brownian motion gives the product ∏n​(1+2λ/((n−1/2)2π2))−1/2. The half-integer cosine product reduces this to (cosh2λ​)−1/2. Expanding at zero gives mean 1/2 and variance 1/3.

Brownian time reversal on a finite interval (Rs​=BT​−BT−s​)

Words: 117 Articles: 1
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For standard Brownian motion and deterministic T>0, the process Rs​=BT​−BT−s​, 0≤s≤T, is standard Brownian motion on that interval in its own natural filtration. Disjoint reversed time intervals give independent centered normal increments with the correct variances. This is different from an arbitrary random-time shift, which can depend on future data. It is also different from the time inversion of Brownian motion transformation tB1/t​.

Independent Brownian arms at a deterministic time

Words: 58
Brownian time reversal on a finite interval OurBigBook.com
For a deterministic h>0, the processes Bh−t​−Bh​, 0≤t≤h, and Bh+t​−Bh​, t≥0, are independent standard Brownian motions. The first uses reversed, sign-changed past increments; the second uses future increments independent of the entire past. The first process is not generally independent of Bh​, but translating a range by Bh​ preserves its Lebesgue measure pathwise.

Longitudinal Brownian field with transverse covariance (E[dBx​(z)dBx​(z′)]=B(z−z′)dx)

Words: 71
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
A longitudinal Brownian field Bx​(z) is a centered Gaussian random field with
E[Bx​(z)Bx′​(z′)]=min(x,x′)B(z−z′),x,x′≥0,
(2)
where B is a valid transverse covariance kernel. For each fixed z it is a scaled Brownian motion, and increments over disjoint longitudinal intervals are independent. Such a field drives a Markov model of wave propagation in a random medium. Its formal longitudinal derivative is Gaussian white noise in x, with transverse correlations described by B; it is not in general a Brownian sheet.

Local maximum of Brownian motion

Words: 48
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
The times of local maxima of a Brownian motion path are dense in the half-line almost surely, and every such local maximum is a strict local maximum. Density follows from nowhere monotonicity of Brownian motion and the extreme value theorem. Strictness follows by checking that maxima over separated rational compact time intervals are unequal; the increment across their gap supplies an independent nondegenerate normal distribution.

Nowhere monotonicity of Brownian motion

Words: 59
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
Almost surely, no restriction of a Brownian motion path to an interval of positive length is a monotone function. On a fixed interval, monotonicity forces the independent centered normal random variables given by every dyadic subdivision's increments to have the same sign. The probability is at most 21−2m for a subdivision into 2m pieces. A countable union over rational intervals gives the simultaneous pathwise assertion.

Brownian hitting of lattice spheres

Words: 109
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For three-dimensional Brownian motion, every radius r>0 and every initial point satisfy
Px​(∃t≥0, z∈Z3: ∣Bt​+z∣=r)=1.
(3)
If the initial point is on one of the spheres, it is already a hit at time zero. If it is inside a lattice-centered open ball, its eventual exit hits that sphere. Otherwise choose at each integer time a nearest lattice center. The current displacement from it has norm at most 3​/2, so the multivariate normal distribution of the next unit increment gives a uniform positive chance of entering its radius-r/2 open ball. The geometric tail bound from a uniform escape probability makes eventual entry certain, and continuity forces a boundary crossing. This periodic-family recurrence does not contradict the Brownian sphere-hitting probability in dimension three for one fixed sphere.

Brownian paths are not uniformly continuous on the half-line

Words: 33
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For every fixed mesh 1/k, independent increments with the normal distribution imply increments of absolute value greater than one occur infinitely often almost surely, by the second Borel-Cantelli lemma. A countable intersection over k contradicts uniform continuity on [0,∞).

Brownian filtration

Words: 89 Articles: 1
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
A filtration (Ft​) is a Brownian filtration for B when B is an adapted process and each future increment Bt​−Bs​ is independent of Fs​. The natural filtration of a Brownian motion has this property. Arbitrary enlargement by future information need not preserve it.

Natural Brownian filtration (FtW​=σ(Ws​:0≤s≤t))

Words: 52
Brownian filtration OurBigBook.com
The natural Brownian filtration is the natural filtration generated by a Brownian motion. Its usual augmentation adds null events and makes it right-continuous; the Brownian martingale representation theorem holds for this augmented natural filtration. A larger Brownian filtration can preserve independence of future increments while containing additional randomness, so it need not have martingale representation with respect to the specified Brownian motion.

Martingale representation theorem

Words: 139 Articles: 2
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
A martingale representation theorem states conditions under which every martingale in a filtration can be represented as a stochastic integral with respect to one or more fundamental martingales.

Brownian martingale representation theorem

Words: 111 Articles: 1
Martingale representation theorem OurBigBook.com
Every square-integrable random variable measurable with respect to a Brownian filtration can be written as its expectation plus an Itô integral against that Brownian motion. Equivalently, every square-integrable martingale in that filtration has the form
Mt​=M0​+∫0t​Hs​dWs​
(4)
for a predictable square-integrable process H.

Clark-Ocone formula for a smooth Brownian terminal payoff (βt​=E[ϕ′(WT​)∣Ft​]1{t≤T}​)

Words: 70
Brownian martingale representation theorem OurBigBook.com
In the completed natural Brownian filtration, a bounded continuously differentiable ϕ with bounded derivative satisfies
ϕ(WT​)=Eϕ(WT​)+∫0T​E[ϕ′(WT​)∣Ft​]dWt​.
(5)
The integrand is unique up to dPdt-almost everywhere equality. Gaussian integration by parts first gives the duality between the payoff and every square-integrable Itô integral. The Brownian martingale representation theorem then identifies the integrand as the projection of ϕ′(WT​)1{t≤T}​ onto the predictable processes in the product L2 space. This explains the conditional expectation in the formula, rather than a nonadapted terminal derivative.

For every θ∈R and standard Brownian motion B,
exp(θBt​−21​θ2t)
(6)

For Brownian motion started at x, the time integral is a Gaussian random variable with
Ex​∫0t​Bs​ds=xt,Var(∫0t​Bs​ds)=3t3​.

Brownian motion transform by three times its running average (Wt​=Wt​−(3/t)∫0t​Ws​ds)

Words: 60
Integral of Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
The displayed continuous centered Gaussian process, with value zero at time zero, has the Brownian covariance kernel. Hence it is a Brownian motion in its own natural filtration. More generally, replacing three by c gives covariance s+c(c−3)(s/2−s2/(6t)) for 0<s≤t, so three is the only nonzero valid coefficient. Its conditional future increment in the original Brownian filtration is 3(t−s)t−1(s−1∫0s​Wu​du−Ws​), and is generally nonzero.

The diffusion coefficient sets the linear growth of mean-square displacement. In one dimension the convention E[(Xt​−X0​)2]=2Dt is common.

Solutal diffusivity (D)

Words: 31
Diffusion coefficient OurBigBook.com
Solutal diffusivity is the diffusion coefficient governing transport of a dissolved constituent down its concentration gradient. For uniform D and a stationary solvent, the diffusion equation is Ct​=D∇2C. It need not equal the thermal diffusivity.

Orthogonal invariance of Brownian motion

Words: 31
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
If B is Brownian motion in Rd and U is an orthogonal matrix, then UB is Brownian motion. Its increments remain independent centered Gaussian vectors and have covariance (t−s)UIUT=(t−s)I.

Meeting time of two independent Brownian motions

Words: 50
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
Two independent one-dimensional Brownian motions started at −a and a meet at the first time a Brownian motion started at 2​a hits zero. The meeting time has density
fT​(u)=πu3​a​e−a2/u,u>0.
(8)
An orthogonal sum coordinate is independent of this hitting time and makes the meeting position conditionally N(0,u/2).

Wiener measure

Words: 249 Articles: 6
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
Wiener measure is the probability distribution of Brownian motion on a continuous-path space, usually C0​([0,T]) or C0​([0,∞)).

Wiener theorem

Words: 62
Wiener measure OurBigBook.com
There exists a probability measure on C0​([0,∞),R) under which the coordinate process is standard Brownian motion, and its distribution there is unique. Construct consistent centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance min(s,t) and use the Kolmogorov extension theorem. The fourth increment moment 3∣t−s∣2 supplies a continuous modification by the Kolmogorov continuity theorem. Its independent increments and normal increment distributions are unchanged. Uniqueness follows because coordinate evaluations at rational times generate the Borel sigma-algebra of continuous-path space.

Words: 564 Articles: 11
Reflection principle (Wiener process) OurBigBook.com
For Mt​=sup0≤s≤t​Bs​, the reflection principle gives
P(Mt​≥x)=2P(Bt​≥x)=P(∣Bt​∣≥x),
(37)
so Mt​ and ∣Bt​∣ have the same distribution.

Gaussian maximal bound for Brownian motion (P(sups≤t​∣Bs​∣>δ)≤2e−δ2/(2t))

Words: 58
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
Stop the Exponential martingale for Brownian motion eθBs​−θ2s/2 when B first reaches δ or at t. On the hitting event its value is at least eθδ−θ2t/2, so that event has probability at most e−θδ+θ2t/2. Minimize over θ>0 and apply the same bound to −B. The union bound gives the displayed inequality for t>0; at zero the probability is zero.

Atomless maxima on separated Brownian intervals (P(sup[a,b]​B=sup[c,d]​B)=0,a<b<c<d)

Words: 69
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
For Brownian motion, write the later maximum as Bb​+Z+H, where Z=Bc​−Bb​ has a nondegenerate normal distribution and H=sup0≤u≤d−c​(Bc+u​−Bc​). The independent increments make Z independent of the earlier history and of H. Conditional on those two objects, equality of the two maxima prescribes one value of Z, an event of probability zero. This argument uses the positive gap c−b and does not assume independence of the two absolute maxima.

Finite-horizon maximum of Brownian motion with drift (Mt​=sups≤t​(Ws​+νs))

Words: 87 Articles: 1
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
For a>0 and t>0, the distribution function is Φ((a−νt)/t​)−e2aνΦ((−a−νt)/t​). The Brownian reflection principle gives the zero-drift terminal density below the barrier as ϕt​(y)−ϕt​(2a−y) for y<a. Weight it by eνy−ν2t/2 using the Girsanov theorem and complete squares in the two Gaussian integrals.
Joint endpoint and maximum law for drifted Brownian motion (P(Wtu​≤x,Mtu​<a))
Words: 43
Finite-horizon maximum of Brownian motion with drift OurBigBook.com
For Wtν​=Bt​+νt, Mtν​=sups≤t​Wsν​, a>0 and x≤a, the joint distribution function is Φ((x−νt)/t​)−e2aνΦ((x−2a−νt)/t​). The Brownian reflection principle gives killed endpoint density ϕt​(y)−ϕt​(2a−y) at zero drift. Multiplication by eνy−ν2t/2 and completion of squares gives the formula.

Integral lower envelope for the Brownian maximum (liminft↓0​St​/(t​f(t))=∞)

Words: 62
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
Let f be positive, continuous and nondecreasing, with ∫01​f(t)dt/t<∞. The small-value probability for the Brownian running maximum is at most a constant times the value. Brownian scaling and dyadic integral comparison make the exceptional probabilities P(S2−n−1​<2−n/2f(2−n)) summable. The Borel-Cantelli first lemma and monotonicity interpolate between dyadic times. Apply this argument to mf for every positive integer m on a countable intersection of probability-one events to obtain the infinite lower limit.

Brownian barrier survival asymptotic (P(sups≤t​Bs​≤h)∼h2/π​t−1/2)

Words: 37
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
For standard one-dimensional Brownian motion and a fixed h>0, the Brownian reflection principle gives the survival probability 2Φ(h/t​)−1. The standard normal distribution function has derivative 1/2π​ at zero, giving the displayed asymptotic. Thus the persistence exponent is one half, with leading constant h2/π​.

Maximum before a lower Brownian barrier (f(x)=(b+x)2b​1{x>0}​)

Words: 42
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
Stopping Brownian motion at its first crossing below −b, the nonnegative local martingale (Wt∧τ​+b)/b starts at one and ends at zero. The maximal identity for a continuous nonnegative local martingale tending to zero gives tail b/(b+x) for the stopped maximum, hence density b/(b+x)2 for x>0. There is no atom at zero.

Joint distribution of Brownian motion and its running maximum

Words: 36
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
Let Mt​=sup0≤s≤t​Bs​ for a standard Brownian motion. For m≥0, the Brownian reflection principle gives
P(Bt​≤b,Mt​≤m)={Φ(b/t​)+Φ((2m−b)/t​)−1,2Φ(m/t​)−1,​b≤m,b>m.​
(38)
On b<m, the pair (Bt​,Mt​) therefore has joint probability density
fBt​,Mt​​(b,m)=2π​t3/22(2m−b)​e−(2m−b)2/(2t).
(39)

Lévy identity for Brownian motion

Words: 35
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
For a standard Brownian motion B, its Brownian running maximum M, and its local time of a semimartingale L0 at zero, the process pairs satisfy
(Mt​−Bt​,Mt​)t≥0​=d(∣Bt​∣,Lt0​)t≥0​.
(40)
In particular, M−B and ∣B∣ are both Reflected Brownian motion and have the same law as processes.

Time of the Brownian maximum (M∗)

Words: 113 Articles: 1
Brownian running maximum OurBigBook.com
Brownian motion attains its maximum on [0,1] at a unique time M∗ almost surely. This time has the arcsine distribution
P(M∗≤s)=π2​arcsins​,0≤s≤1.
(41)
Brownian motion shifted at its finite-horizon maximum (Yt​=Bτ+t​−Bτ​)
Words: 86
Time of the Brownian maximum OurBigBook.com
Let τ be the first attainment of the maximum of standard Brownian motion on [0,T], with T>0. Time reversal shows τ<T with probability one. Then Yt​≤0 for 0≤t≤T−τ, an initial interval of positive length. Standard Brownian motion has probability zero of this property by the Brownian reflection principle, so Y is not Brownian. Moreover τ is not a stopping time for the natural Brownian filtration: for 0<t<T, P(τ≤t∣Ft​)=2Φ((Mt​−Bt​)/T−t​)−1, which is strictly between zero and one on {Bt​<0}. The Strong Markov property is therefore inapplicable at this random time.

Brownian transition semigroup

Words: 113 Articles: 3
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For suitable f,
(Pt​f)(x)=E[f(x+t​Z)]
(42)
defines the Brownian transition semigroup. Its generator identity is
dtd​Pt​f=21​Pt​f′′.
(43)
Each Gaussian-convolution operator is a rescaled Weierstrass transform; the semigroup combines all times.

Brownian transition density (pt​(x,y))

Words: 57 Articles: 1
Brownian transition semigroup OurBigBook.com
The transition density of standard Brownian motion in Rd is the heat kernel
pt​(x,y)=(2πt)d/21​exp(−2t∣y−x∣2​),t>0.
(44)
Thus Px​(Xt​∈A)=∫A​pt​(x,y)dy.

Killed Brownian transition density (pD​(t,z,w))

Words: 35
Brownian transition density OurBigBook.com
The area density of Pz​(Bt​∈dw, t<TD​) for planar Brownian motion killed on its first exit from D. Its total mass is the survival probability, not generally one. Integrating this density over time gives the Green function of killed planar Brownian motion.

Brownian compensator martingale

Words: 26
Brownian transition semigroup OurBigBook.com
For a twice differentiable integrable test function f and Brownian motion W,
f(Wt​)−21​∫0t​f′′(Ws​)ds
(45)
is a martingale. This is the one-dimensional generator form of Dynkin's formula.

Exponential test-function characterization of Brownian motion

Words: 91 Articles: 1
Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
Let W be continuous with W0​=0. If
ecWt​−2c2​∫0t​ecWs​ds
(46)
is a martingale for every real c, then conditional expectations solve
E[ecWt​∣Fs​]=ecWs​+c2(t−s)/2.
(47)
Thus Wt​−Ws​ is independent of Fs​ and distributed as N(0,t−s), so W is Brownian motion.

Conditional characteristic-function criterion for Brownian increments (E[eiθ(Xt​−Xs​)∣Fs​]=e−θ2(t−s)/2)

Words: 49
Exponential test-function characterization of Brownian motion OurBigBook.com
For an adapted continuous process starting at zero, the displayed conditional characteristic function identifies every increment as N(0,t−s) and makes it independent of the preceding sigma-field. Multiply by the indicator of an event in that sigma-field, then use the uniqueness theorem for characteristic functions for finite measures. Thus the process is a Brownian motion in the given filtration.
